evidence: Fresh tests.ai.test_model_registry proves exact pins, task/features/modalities/context/resource limits, evaluation observations, current policy/rights binding, classification/egress/budget denials and default-deny behavior. Its actual 1,000-manifest deterministic matcher benchmark asserts filtering/ranking below 100 ms. Eligible candidates explicitly confer no execution permission; CAP-07.S01.T03 must reauthorize at dispatch.

Fresh protected SQLCipher repository tests prove versioned immutable history, process-object reconstruction, lost availability after reconstruction, monotonic manifest revisions including removed entries, CAS concurrency, idempotent identical command replay, changed-key conflicts, atomic failure rollback, wrong-project/actor rejection, 1,000-model persistence and corrupt-latest rejection. No fake installed models ship; production inventory defaults empty.

Fresh actual generated TypeScript client over authenticated loopback HTTP to Core and protected project storage proves read/refresh/replay and bearer/actor-spoof denial. API tests prove read-only/closed rejection, bounded manifest/history pagination, historical reads and safe projections. Model Center exposes versions, identity/capability/license/resource/evaluation metadata and honest current/empty/unavailable states without installing or executing a model.

Fresh Python AI/service/repository/contract and affected runtime/auth tests passed. Generated-client tests reject extra/hostile metadata and substituted hashes. Native Rust tests independently enforce exact process-bound handshake and catalog route/method/header/body allowlists, including forged authority and duplicate JSON keys.

Fresh production-bundle Playwright fixture test exercises closed, populated, empty, failure and late-result states, keyboard traversal, long model identity reflow at 1440/1280/720 widths and both themes. Full affected shell test retains all prior workspaces, adds the ninth, and checks project/workflow context, style primitives, keyboard/focus, error recovery and responsive geometry. These synthetic headless browser checks are not Windows-native interaction proof.

Fresh TypeScript component/navigation/runtime tests, strict type checks, desktop lint/build, changed Python Ruff checks, narrow new-Core mypy, deterministic generation, schema/quality inventories, architecture and generated backlog views all passed at the candidate. Each checks entry records actual command, duration, exit code and output hash, not an inferred or reused result.

The public manifest schema, Core OpenAPI/client, native/benchmark capability inventories and product build identity are updated consistently. Existing protected settings/audit/outbox schema is reused without a migration. Core derives actor authority and never accepts model/permission flags from the renderer. The architecture/contract documentation and approved-reference mapping explain default-empty inventory, task-policy requirements and future execution boundaries.

One reusable opt-in wrapping utility fixes the observed long-identifier overflow; existing controls, tokens and shared layout are reused. No governed reference changes or optional styling gate is introduced. Quality scope registers ten new Python files; build schema inventory also corrects an already-existing v4.1 schema omission without changing that schema or its authority.

Public OpenAPI digest equality was verified after a credential-scanner false positive; its exported constant remains compatible via an explicitly named digest. New/affected synthetic authentication fixtures use ephemeral tokens. Normal commit privacy hooks passed with no scanner, sealed-admission or baseline change. The protected historical witness and excluded sibling were not accessed.
